descriptions.value: It was noticed an XSS in certain 404 pages that could be exploited to perform an XSS attack. Chrome will detect this as a reflected XSS attempt and prevent the page from loading. Firefox and other browsers don't, and are vulnerable to this attack. Mitigation: The fix for this is to upgrade to Apache Airflow 1.9.0 or above.

Se ha descubierto Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) en ciertas páginas 404 que podría explotarse para realizar un ataque de Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). Chrome lo detectará como un intento de Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) reflejado y evitará que la página se cargue. Firefox y otros navegadores no, por lo que son vulnerables a este ataque. Mitigación: la solución a este problema es actualizar a Apache Airflow 1.9.0 o siguientes.
In Apache Airflow 1.8.2 and earlier, an authenticated user can execute code remotely on the Airflow webserver by creating a special object.
En Apache Airflow, en versiones 1.8.2 y anteriores, un usuario autenticado puede ejecutar código de forma remota en el servidor web de Airflow mediante la creación de un objeto especial.
In Apache Airflow 1.8.2 and earlier, a CSRF vulnerability allowed for a remote command injection on a default install of Airflow.
En Apache Airflow, en versiones 1.8.2 y anteriores, una vulnerabilidad de Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) permitía la inyección remota de comandos en una instalación por defecto de Airflow.

In Apache Airflow 1.8.2 and earlier, an experimental Airflow feature displayed authenticated cookies, as well as passwords to databases used by Airflow. An attacker who has limited access to airflow, whether it be via XSS or by leaving a machine unlocked can exfiltrate all credentials from the system.

En Apache Airflow versión 1.8.2 y anteriores, una función experimental de Airflow mostraba cookies identificadas, así como contraseñas a las bases de datos utilizadas por Airflow. Un atacante que presenta acceso limitado a Airflow, ya sea por medio  de Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) o al dejar una máquina desbloqueada puede eliminar todas las credenciales del sistema.

The LDAP auth backend (airflow.contrib.auth.backends.ldap_auth) prior to Apache Airflow 1.10.1 was misconfigured and contained improper checking of exceptions which disabled server certificate checking.

El backend de autenticación LDAP (airflow.contrib.auth.backends.ldap_auth), en versiones anteriores a Apache Airflow 1.10.1, se configuró erróneamente y contenía una comprobación incorrecta de excepciones que deshabilitaban la comprobación de certificados del servidor.
In Apache Airflow before 1.10.2, a malicious admin user could edit the state of objects in the Airflow metadata database to execute arbitrary javascript on certain page views.

En Apache Airflow, en versiones anteriores a la 1.10.2, un administrador malicioso podría editar el estado de objetos en la base de datos de los metadatos de Airflow para ejecutar JavaScript arbitrario en determinadas vistas de páginas.
A malicious admin user could edit the state of objects in the Airflow metadata database to execute arbitrary javascript on certain page views.
Un usuario administrador malicioso podría editar el estado de los objetos en la base de datos metadata de Airflow para ejecutar JavaScript arbitrario en determinadas vistas de páginas.
A number of HTTP endpoints in the Airflow webserver (both RBAC and classic) did not have adequate protection and were vulnerable to cross-site request forgery attacks.
Varios endpoints HTTP en el webserver Airflow (tanto RBAC como clásico) no tenían la protección adecuada y eran vulnerables a los ataques de tipo cross-site request forgery (CSRF)

A malicious admin user could edit the state of objects in the Airflow metadata database to execute arbitrary javascript on certain page views. This also presented a Local File Disclosure vulnerability to any file readable by the webserver process.

Un usuario administrador malicioso podría editar el estado de los objetos en la base de datos de metadatos de Airflow para ejecutar JavaScript arbitrario en determinadas vistas de página. Esto también presentó una vulnerabilidad de Divulgación de Archivos Local en cualquier archivo legible por el proceso del servidor web.

In Apache Airflow before 1.10.5 when running with the "classic" UI, a malicious admin user could edit the state of objects in the Airflow metadata database to execute arbitrary javascript on certain page views. The new "RBAC" UI is unaffected.

En Apache Airflow versiones anteriores a 1.10.5, cuando se ejecuta con la interfaz de usuario "clasic", un usuario administrador malicioso podía editar el estado de los objetos en la base de datos de metadatos de Airflow para ejecutar javascript arbitrario en determinadas vistas de página. La nueva Interfaz de Usuario "RBAC" no está afectada.

An issue was found in Apache Airflow versions 1.10.10 and below. A remote code/command injection vulnerability was discovered in one of the example DAGs shipped with Airflow which would allow any authenticated user to run arbitrary commands as the user running airflow worker/scheduler (depending on the executor in use). If you already have examples disabled by setting load_examples=False in the config then you are not vulnerable.

Se encontró un problema en Apache Airflow versiones 1.10.10 y posteriores. Se detectó una vulnerabilidad de inyección de código y comando remota en uno de los DAG de ejemplo enviados con Airflow que permitiría a cualquier usuario autenticado ejecutar comandos arbitrarios como el usuario que ejecuta el programador y trabajador de airflow (dependiendo del ejecutor en uso). Si ya presentas ejemplos deshabilitados al configurar la función  load_examples=False en la configuración, entonces no es vulnerable

An issue was found in Apache Airflow versions 1.10.10 and below. When using CeleryExecutor, if an attacker can connect to the broker (Redis, RabbitMQ) directly, it is possible to inject commands, resulting in the celery worker running arbitrary commands.

Se encontró un problema en Apache Airflow versiones 1.10.10 y posteriores. Cuando se usa la función CeleryExecutor, si un atacante puede conectarse directamente al broker (Redis, RabbitMQ), es posible inyectar comandos, resultando que el trabajador de celery ejecuta comandos arbitrarios

An issue was found in Apache Airflow versions 1.10.10 and below. When using CeleryExecutor, if an attack can connect to the broker (Redis, RabbitMQ) directly, it was possible to insert a malicious payload directly to the broker which could lead to a deserialization attack (and thus remote code execution) on the Worker.

Se encontró un problema en Apache Airflow versiones 1.10.10 y posteriores. Cuando se usa la función CeleryExecutor, si un ataque puede conectarse directamente al broker (Redis, RabbitMQ), era posible insertar una carga maliciosa directamente al agente que podría conllevar a un ataque de deserialización (y, por lo tanto, a un ejecución de código remota) en el Worker

An issue was found in Apache Airflow versions 1.10.10 and below. It was discovered that many of the admin management screens in the new/RBAC UI handled escaping incorrectly, allowing authenticated users with appropriate permissions to create stored XSS attacks.

Se encontró un problema en Apache Airflow versiones 1.10.10 y posteriores. Se detectó que muchas de las pantallas de gestión de administración en la UI new/RBAC manejaban el escape incorrectamente, permitiendo a usuarios autenticados con los permisos apropiados crear ataques de tipo XSS almacenado
An issue was found in Apache Airflow versions 1.10.10 and below. A stored XSS vulnerability was discovered in the Chart pages of the the "classic" UI.
Se encontró un problema en Apache Airflow versiones 1.10.10 y posteriores. Se detectó una vulnerabilidad de tipo XSS almacenado en las páginas de Chart de la IU "classic"
In Apache Airflow < 1.10.12, the "origin" parameter passed to some of the endpoints like '/trigger' was vulnerable to XSS exploit.
En Apache Airflow versiones anteriores a 1.10.12, el parámetro "origin" pasado a algunos de los endpoints como "/trigger" era vulnerable a una explotación de un XSS

The previous default setting for Airflow's Experimental API was to allow all API requests without authentication, but this poses security risks to users who miss this fact. From Airflow 1.10.11 the default has been changed to deny all requests by default and is documented at https://airflow.apache.org/docs/1.10.11/security.html#api-authentication. Note this change fixes it for new installs but existing users need to change their config to default `[api]auth_backend = airflow.api.auth.backend.deny_all` as mentioned in the Updating Guide: https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/1.10.11/UPDATING.md#experimental-api-will-deny-all-request-by-default

La configuración predeterminada previa para Airflow's Experimental API permitió todas las peticiones de la API sin autenticación, pero esto plantea riesgos de seguridad para los usuarios que no se dan cuenta de este hecho. Desde Airflow versión 1.10.11, el valor predeterminado ha sido cambiado para denegar todas las peticiones por defecto y está documentado en https://airflow.apache.org/docs/1.10.11/security.html#api-authentication. Tome en cuenta que este cambio lo corrige para nuevas instalaciones, pero los usuarios existentes deben cambiar su configuración a la predeterminada "[api] auth_backend=airflow.api.auth.backend.deny_all" como es mencionado en la Guía de Actualización: https://github.com/apache /airflow/blob/1.10.11/UPDATING.md#experimental-api-will-deny-all-request-by-defaul

cve.cisaVulnerabilityName: Apache Airflow's Experimental API Authentication Bypass

descriptions.value: The "origin" parameter passed to some of the endpoints like '/trigger' was vulnerable to XSS exploit. This issue affects Apache Airflow versions prior to 1.10.13. This is same as CVE-2020-13944 but the implemented fix in Airflow 1.10.13 did not fix the issue completely.

El parámetro "origin" pasado a algunos de los endpoints como "/trigger" era vulnerable a una explotación de XSS. Este problema afecta a Apache Airflow versiones anteriores a 1.10.13. Es lo mismo que CVE-2020-13944, pero la corrección implementada en Airflow versión 1.10.13 no corrigió el problema completamente

In Airflow versions prior to 1.10.13, when creating a user using airflow CLI, the password gets logged in plain text in the Log table in Airflow Metadatase. Same happened when creating a Connection with a password field.

En Airflow versiones anteriores a 1.10.13, cuando se crea un usuario usando la CLI de airflow, la contraseña se registra en texto plano en la tabla de Registro en Airflow Metadatase. Lo mismo sucedió cuando se creó una Conexión con un campo de contraseña.
In Apache Airflow versions prior to 1.10.13, the Charts and Query View of the old (Flask-admin based) UI were vulnerable for SSRF attack.
En Apache Airflow versiones anteriores a 1.10.13, los Gráficos y la Visualización de Consulta de la antigua interfaz del usuario (basada en Flask-admin) eran vulnerables a un ataque de tipo SSRF.

Incorrect Session Validation in Apache Airflow Webserver versions prior to 1.10.14 with default config allows a malicious airflow user on site A where they log in normally, to access unauthorized Airflow Webserver on Site B through the session from Site A. This does not affect users who have changed the default value for `[webserver] secret_key` config.

La Comprobación de Sesión Incorrecta en Apache Airflow Webserver versiones anteriores a 1.10.14, con la configuración predeterminada permite a un usuario de airflow malicioso en el sitio A donde inician sesión normalmente para el acceso no autorizado a Airflow Webserver en el Sitio B mediante la sesión del sitio A. Esto no afecta a usuarios que han cambiado el valor predeterminado para la configuración de "(webserver) secret_key"

Improper Access Control on Configurations Endpoint for the Stable API of Apache Airflow allows users with Viewer or User role to get Airflow Configurations including sensitive information even when `[webserver] expose_config` is set to `False` in `airflow.cfg`. This allowed a privilege escalation attack. This issue affects Apache Airflow 2.0.0.

Un Control de Acceso Inapropiado en el Endpoint Configurations para la API Stable de Apache Airflow permite a usuarios con rol de Visualizadores o Usuario obtener Configuraciones de Airflow, incluyendo información confidencial, incluso cuando "[webserver] expose_config" está configurado como "False" en "airflow.cfg". Esto permitió un ataque de escalada de privilegios. Este problema afecta a Apache Airflow versión 2.0.0

The lineage endpoint of the deprecated Experimental API was not protected by authentication in Airflow 2.0.0. This allowed unauthenticated users to hit that endpoint. This is low-severity issue as the attacker needs to be aware of certain parameters to pass to that endpoint and even after can just get some metadata about a DAG and a Task. This issue affects Apache Airflow 2.0.0.

El endpoint lineage de la API Experimental obsoleta no estaba protegido por autenticación en Airflow versión 2.0.0. Esto permitió a usuarios no autenticados llegar a ese endpoint. Este es un problema de baja gravedad, ya que el atacante debe estar consciente de determinados parámetros para pasar a ese endpoint e incluso después puede obtener algunos metadatos sobre un DAG y una tarea. Este problema afecta a Apache Airflow versión 2.0.0

The "origin" parameter passed to some of the endpoints like '/trigger' was vulnerable to XSS exploit. This issue affects Apache Airflow versions <1.10.15 in 1.x series and affects 2.0.0 and 2.0.1 and 2.x series. This is the same as CVE-2020-13944 & CVE-2020-17515 but the implemented fix did not fix the issue completely. Update to Airflow 1.10.15 or 2.0.2. Please also update your Python version to the latest available PATCH releases of the installed MINOR versions, example update to Python 3.6.13 if you are on Python 3.6. (Those contain the fix for CVE-2021-23336 https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-23336).

El parámetro "origin" pasado a algunos de los endpoints como "/trigger" era vulnerable a una explotación de tipo XSS. Este problema afecta a Apache Airflow versiones anteriores a 1.10.15 en la serie 1.x y afecta a las series 2.0.0 y 2.0.1 y 2.x. Es lo mismo que CVE-2020-13944 y CVE-2020-17515, pero la corrección implementada no corrigió el problema por completo. Actualice a Airflow versiones 1.10.15 o 2.0.2. Actualice también su versión de Python a las últimas versiones de PATCH disponibles de las versiones MINOR instaladas, ejemplo de actualización a Python versión 3.6.13 si está en Python versión 3.6. (Estos contienen la corrección para CVE-2021-23336 https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-23336).

If remote logging is not used, the worker (in the case of CeleryExecutor) or the scheduler (in the case of LocalExecutor) runs a Flask logging server and is listening on a specific port and also binds on 0.0.0.0 by default. This logging server had no authentication and allows reading log files of DAG jobs. This issue affects Apache Airflow < 2.1.2.

Si no es usado el registro remoto, el trabajador (en el caso de CeleryExecutor) o el planificador (en el caso de LocalExecutor) ejecuta un servidor de registro Flask y está escuchando en un puerto específico y también se vincula en 0.0.0.0 por defecto. Este servidor de registro no presenta autenticación y permite leer los archivos de registro de los trabajos DAG. Este problema afecta a Apache Airflow versiones anteriores a 2.1.2.

The variable import endpoint was not protected by authentication in Airflow >=2.0.0, <2.1.3. This allowed unauthenticated users to hit that endpoint to add/modify Airflow variables used in DAGs, potentially resulting in a denial of service, information disclosure or remote code execution. This issue affects Apache Airflow >=2.0.0, <2.1.3.

El endpoint de importación de variables no estaba protegido por autenticación en Airflow versiones posteriores a 2.0.0 incluyéndola, versiones anteriores a 2.1.3. Esto permitía a usuarios no autenticados acceder a ese endpoint para añadir y modificar las variables de Airflow usadas en los DAG, resultando en una denegación de servicio, una divulgación de información o una ejecución de código remota. Este problema afecta a Apache Airflow versiones posteriores a 2.0.0 incluyéndola, versiones anteriores a 2.1.3

In Apache Airflow prior to 2.2.0. This CVE applies to a specific case where a User who has "can_create" permissions on DAG Runs can create Dag Runs for dags that they don't have "edit" permissions for.

En Apache Airflow versiones anteriores a 2.2.0. Esta CVE es aplicada a un caso específico en el que un usuario que presenta permisos "can_create" en las ejecuciones DAG puede crear ejecuciones Dag para dags para los que no presenta permisos "edit"
It was discovered that the "Trigger DAG with config" screen was susceptible to XSS attacks via the `origin` query argument. This issue affects Apache Airflow versions 2.2.3 and below.

Se ha detectado que la pantalla "Trigger DAG with config" era susceptible de ataques de tipo XSS por medio del argumento de consulta "origin". Este problema afecta a Apache Airflow versiones 2.2.3 y anteriores.
In Apache Airflow, prior to version 2.2.4, some example DAGs did not properly sanitize user-provided params, making them susceptible to OS Command Injection from the web UI.

En Apache Airflow, versiones anteriores a 2.2.4, algunos DAG de ejemplo no saneaban correctamente los parámetros proporcionados por el usuario, lo que los hacía susceptibles a inyección de comandos del Sistema Operativo desde la interfaz web.
Apache Airflow Docker's Provider prior to 3.0.0 shipped with an example DAG that was vulnerable to (authenticated) remote code exploit of code on the Airflow worker host.
El Proveedor de Apache Airflow Docker versiones anteriores a 3.0.0, incluía un ejemplo de DAG que era vulnerable a una explotación remota (autenticada) de código en el host del trabajador de Airflow.
In Apache Airflow versions 2.2.4 through 2.3.3, the `database` webserver session backend was susceptible to session fixation.
En Apache Airflow versiones 2.2.4 hasta 2.3.3, el backend de sesión del servidor web "database" era susceptible a una fijación de sesión

In Apache Airflow prior to 2.3.4, an insecure umask was configured for numerous Airflow components when running with the `--daemon` flag which could result in a race condition giving world-writable files in the Airflow home directory and allowing local users to expose arbitrary file contents via the webserver.

En Apache Airflow versiones anteriores a 2.3.4, era configurado una máscara de usuario no segura para numerosos componentes de Airflow cuando es ejecutado con el flag "--daemon", lo que podía resultar en una condición de carrera que daba lugar a archivos de escritura mundial en el directorio principal de Airflow y permitía a usuarios locales exponer contenidos de archivos arbitrarios por medio del servidor web
In Apache Airflow 2.3.0 through 2.3.4, part of a url was unnecessarily formatted, allowing for possible information extraction.
En Apache Airflow versiones 2.3.0 hasta 2.3.4, parte de una url tenía un formato no necesario que permitía una posible extracción de información
In Apache Airflow 2.3.0 through 2.3.4, there was an open redirect in the webserver's `/confirm` endpoint.
En Apache Airflow versiones 2.3.0 hasta 2.3.4, se presentaba un redireccionamiento abierto en el endpoint "/confirm" del servidor web
In Apache Airflow, prior to version 2.4.1, deactivating a user wouldn't prevent an already authenticated user from being able to continue using the UI or API.
En Apache Airflow, versiones anteriores a 2.4.1, desactivar un usuario no impedía que un usuario ya autenticado pudiera seguir usando la Interfaz de Usuario o la API
In Apache Airflow versions prior to 2.4.2, the "Trigger DAG with config" screen was susceptible to XSS attacks via the `origin` query argument.
En las versiones de Apache Airflow anteriores a la 2.4.2, la pantalla "Trigger DAG with config" era susceptible a ataques XSS a través del argumento de consulta "origin".
In Apache Airflow versions prior to 2.4.2, there was an open redirect in the webserver's `/confirm` endpoint.
En las versiones de Apache Airflow anteriores a la 2.4.2, había una redirección abierta en el punto final `/confirm` del servidor web.

A vulnerability in UI of Apache Airflow allows an attacker to view unmasked secrets in rendered template values for tasks which were not executed (for example when they were depending on past and previous instances of the task failed). This issue affects Apache Airflow prior to 2.3.1.

Una vulnerabilidad en la interfaz de usuario de Apache Airflow permite a un atacante ver secretos desenmascarados en valores de plantilla representados para tareas que no se ejecutaron (por ejemplo, cuando dependían de instancias pasadas y anteriores de la tarea que fallaron). Este problema afecta a Apache Airflow antes de la versión 2.3.1.

A vulnerability in Example Dags of Apache Airflow allows an attacker with UI access who can trigger DAGs, to execute arbitrary commands via manually provided run_id parameter. This issue affects Apache Airflow Apache Airflow versions prior to 2.4.0.

Una vulnerabilidad en Dags de ejemplo de Apache Airflow permite a un atacante con acceso a la interfaz de usuario que puede activar DAG ejecutar comandos arbitrarios a través del parámetro run_id proporcionado manualmente. Este problema afecta a las versiones de Apache Airflow Apache Airflow anteriores a la 2.4.0.
In Apache Airflow versions prior to 2.4.3, there was an open redirect in the webserver's `/login` endpoint.
En las versiones de Apache Airflow anteriores a la 2.4.3, había una redirección abierta en el endpoint `/login` del servidor web.

Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection') vulnerability in Apache Airflow Pinot Provider, Apache Airflow allows an attacker to control commands executed in the task execution context, without write access to DAG files. This issue affects Apache Airflow Pinot Provider versions prior to 4.0.0. It also impacts any Apache Airflow versions prior to 2.3.0 in case Apache Airflow Pinot Provider is installed (Apache Airflow Pinot Provider 4.0.0 can only be installed for Airflow 2.3.0+). Note that you need to manually install the Pinot Provider version 4.0.0 in order to get rid of the vulnerability on top of Airflow 2.3.0+ version.

Neutralización inadecuada de elementos especiales utilizados en una vulnerabilidad de comando del sistema operativo ('inyección de comando del sistema operativo') en el proveedor Apache Airflow Pinot. Apache Airflow permite a un atacante controlar los comandos ejecutados en el contexto de ejecución de la tarea, sin acceso de escritura a los archivos DAG. Este problema afecta a las versiones del proveedor Apache Airflow Pinot anteriores a la 4.0.0. También afecta a cualquier versión de Apache Airflow anterior a la 2.3.0 en caso de que Apache Airflow Pinot Provider esté instalado (Apache Airflow Pinot Provider 4.0.0 solo se puede instalar para Airflow 2.3.0+). Tenga en cuenta que debe instalar manualmente Pinot Provider versión 4.0.0 para eliminar la vulnerabilidad además de la versión Airflow 2.3.0+.

Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection') vulnerability in Apache Airflow Pig Provider, Apache Airflow allows an attacker to control commands executed in the task execution context, without write access to DAG files. This issue affects Pig Provider versions prior to 4.0.0. It also impacts any Apache Airflow versions prior to 2.3.0 in case Pig Provider is installed (Pig Provider 4.0.0 can only be installed for Airflow 2.3.0+). Note that you need to manually install the Pig Provider version 4.0.0 in order to get rid of the vulnerability on top of Airflow 2.3.0+ version.

Neutralización inadecuada de elementos especiales utilizados en una vulnerabilidad de comando del sistema operativo ('inyección de comando del sistema operativo') en Apache Airflow Pig Provider, Apache Airflow permite a un atacante controlar los comandos ejecutados en el contexto de ejecución de la tarea, sin acceso de escritura a los archivos DAG. Este problema afecta a las versiones de Pig Provider anteriores a la 4.0.0. También afecta cualquier versión de Apache Airflow anterior a la 2.3.0 en caso de que Pig Provider esté instalado (Pig Provider 4.0.0 solo se puede instalar para Airflow 2.3.0+). Tenga en cuenta que debe instalar manualmente Pig Provider versión 4.0.0 para eliminar la vulnerabilidad además de la versión Airflow 2.3.0+.

Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection') vulnerability in Apache Airflow Spark Provider, Apache Airflow allows an attacker to read arbtrary files in the task execution context, without write access to DAG files. This issue affects Spark Provider versions prior to 4.0.0. It also impacts any Apache Airflow versions prior to 2.3.0 in case Spark Provider is installed (Spark Provider 4.0.0 can only be installed for Airflow 2.3.0+). Note that you need to manually install the Spark Provider version 4.0.0 in order to get rid of the vulnerability on top of Airflow 2.3.0+ version that has lower version of the Spark Provider installed).

Neutralización inadecuada de elementos especiales utilizados en una vulnerabilidad de comando del sistema operativo ('inyección de comando del sistema operativo') en Apache Airflow Spark Provider. Apache Airflow permite a un atacante leer archivos arbitrarios en el contexto de ejecución de la tarea, sin acceso de escritura a los archivos DAG. Este problema afecta a las versiones del proveedor Spark anteriores a la 4.0.0. También afecta cualquier versión de Apache Airflow anterior a la 2.3.0 en caso de que Spark Provider esté instalado (Spark Provider 4.0.0 solo se puede instalar para Airflow 2.3.0+). Tenga en cuenta que debe instalar manualmente Spark Provider versión 4.0.0 para eliminar la vulnerabilidad además de la versión Airflow 2.3.0+ que tiene instalada una versión inferior de Spark Provider).

Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection') vulnerability in Apache Airflow Hive Provider, Apache Airflow allows an attacker to execute arbtrary commands in the task execution context, without write access to DAG files. This issue affects Hive Provider versions prior to 4.1.0. It also impacts any Apache Airflow versions prior to 2.3.0 in case HIve Provider is installed (Hive Provider 4.1.0 can only be installed for Airflow 2.3.0+). Note that you need to manually install the HIve Provider version 4.1.0 in order to get rid of the vulnerability on top of Airflow 2.3.0+ version that has lower version of the Hive Provider installed).

Neutralización inadecuada de elementos especiales utilizados en una vulnerabilidad de comando del sistema operativo ('inyección de comando del sistema operativo') en Apache Airflow Hive Provider, Apache Airflow permite a un atacante ejecutar comandos arbitrarios en el contexto de ejecución de la tarea, sin acceso de escritura a los archivos DAG. Este problema afecta a las versiones del proveedor Hive anteriores a la 4.1.0. También afecta cualquier versión de Apache Airflow anterior a la 2.3.0 en caso de que esté instalado HIve Provider (Hive Provider 4.1.0 solo se puede instalar para Airflow 2.3.0+). Tenga en cuenta que debe instalar manualmente la versión 4.1.0 del proveedor Hive para eliminar la vulnerabilidad además de la versión 2.3.0+ de Airflow que tiene instalada una versión inferior del proveedor Hive).

Due to improper restriction, authenticated attackers could retrieve and read system files of the underlying server through the XML interface. The information that can be read can lead to a full system compromise.
Debido a una restricción inadecuada, los atacantes podían recuperar y leer archivos de sistema del servidor subyacente a través de la interfaz XML.

descriptions.value:
A vulnerability was found in Undertow. This vulnerability impacts a server that supports the wildfly-http-client protocol. Whenever a malicious user opens and closes a connection with the HTTP port of the server and then closes the connection immediately, the server will end with both memory and open file limits exhausted at some point, depending on the amount of memory available. 

At HTTP upgrade to remoting, the WriteTimeoutStreamSinkConduit leaks connections if RemotingConnection is closed by Remoting ServerConnectionOpenListener. Because the remoting connection originates in Undertow as part of the HTTP upgrade, there is an external layer to the remoting connection. This connection is unaware of the outermost layer when closing the connection during the connection opening procedure. Hence, the Undertow WriteTimeoutStreamSinkConduit is not notified of the closed connection in this scenario. Because WriteTimeoutStreamSinkConduit creates a timeout task, the whole dependency tree leaks via that task, which is added to XNIO WorkerThread. So, the workerThread points to the Undertow conduit, which contains the connections and causes the leak.

Se encontró una vulnerabilidad en Undertow. Esta vulnerabilidad afecta a un servidor que admite el protocolo wildfly-http-client. Siempre que un usuario malintencionado abre y cierra una conexión con el puerto HTTP del servidor y luego cierra la conexión inmediatamente, el servidor finalizará con los límites de memoria y de archivos abiertos agotados en algún momento, dependiendo de la cantidad de memoria disponible. En la actualización HTTP a comunicación remota, WriteTimeoutStreamSinkConduit pierde conexiones si RemotingConnection se cierra mediante Remoting ServerConnectionOpenListener. Debido a que la conexión remota se origina en Undertow como parte de la actualización HTTP, existe una capa externa a la conexión remota. Esta conexión desconoce la capa más externa al cerrar la conexión durante el procedimiento de apertura de la conexión. Por lo tanto, Undertow WriteTimeoutStreamSinkConduit no recibe notificación de la conexión cerrada en este escenario. Debido a que WriteTimeoutStreamSinkConduit crea una tarea de tiempo de espera, todo el árbol de dependencia se filtra a través de esa tarea, que se agrega a XNIO WorkerThread. Entonces, el hilo de trabajo apunta al conducto Undertow, que contiene las conexiones y causa la fuga.

descriptions.value: A vulnerability was found in Undertow where the ProxyProtocolReadListener reuses the same StringBuilder instance across multiple requests. This issue occurs when the parseProxyProtocolV1 method processes multiple requests on the same HTTP connection. As a result, different requests may share the same StringBuilder instance, potentially leading to information leakage between requests or responses. In some cases, a value from a previous request or response may be erroneously reused, which could lead to unintended data exposure. This issue primarily results in errors and connection termination but creates a risk of data leakage in multi-request environments.

Se encontró una vulnerabilidad en Undertow donde ProxyProtocolReadListener reutiliza la misma instancia de StringBuilder en múltiples solicitudes. Este problema ocurre cuando el método parseProxyProtocolV1 procesa múltiples solicitudes en la misma conexión HTTP. Como resultado, diferentes solicitudes pueden compartir la misma instancia de StringBuilder, lo que podría provocar una fuga de información entre solicitudes o respuestas. En algunos casos, un valor de una solicitud o respuesta anterior puede reutilizarse por error, lo que podría provocar una exposición no deseada de los datos. Este problema produce principalmente errores y terminación de la conexión, pero crea un riesgo de fuga de datos en entornos de solicitudes múltiples.

descriptions.value: DOMPurify is a DOM-only, super-fast, uber-tolerant XSS sanitizer for HTML, MathML and SVG. It has been discovered that malicious HTML using special nesting techniques can bypass the depth checking added to DOMPurify in recent releases. It was also possible to use Prototype Pollution to weaken the depth check. This renders dompurify unable to avoid cross site scripting (XSS) attacks. This issue has been addressed in versions 2.5.4 and 3.1.3 of DOMPurify. All users are advised to upgrade. There are no known workarounds for this vulnerability.

DOMPurify es un desinfectante XSS ultrarrápido, ultratolerante y exclusivo de DOM para HTML, MathML y SVG. Se ha descubierto que el HTML malicioso que utiliza técnicas de anidación especiales puede eludir la comprobación de profundidad agregada a DOMPurify en versiones recientes. También fue posible utilizar Prototype Pollution para debilitar la comprobación de profundidad. Esto hace que dompurify no pueda evitar los ataques de cross site scripting (XSS). Este problema se ha solucionado en las versiones 2.5.4 y 3.1.3 de DOMPurify. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios que actualicen. No existen workarounds para esta vulnerabilidad.

A vulnerability was found in Golang FIPS OpenSSL. This flaw allows a malicious user to randomly cause an uninitialized buffer length variable with a zeroed buffer to be returned in FIPS mode. It may also be possible to force a false positive match between non-equal hashes when comparing a trusted computed hmac sum to an untrusted input sum if an attacker can send a zeroed buffer in place of a pre-computed sum.  It is also possible to force a derived key to be all zeros instead of an unpredictable value.  This may have follow-on implications for the Go TLS stack.

Se encontró una vulnerabilidad en Golang FIPS OpenSSL. Esta falla permite que un usuario malintencionado haga que se devuelva aleatoriamente una variable de longitud de búfer no inicializada con un búfer puesto a cero en modo FIPS. También es posible forzar una coincidencia de falso positivo entre hashes no iguales al comparar una suma hmac calculada confiable con una suma de entrada no confiable si un atacante puede enviar un búfer puesto a cero en lugar de una suma calculada previamente. También es posible forzar que una clave derivada sea todo ceros en lugar de un valor impredecible. Esto puede tener implicaciones posteriores para la pila TLS de Go.

A flaw was found in the interaction between systemd-gpt-auto-generator and 
confidential computing guest VM images in OpenShift Sandboxed Containers 
(confidential peer pods). systemd-gpt-auto-generator automatically discovers 
and mounts GPT partitions by type GUID at boot with no user confirmation. In 
the confidential computing threat model, where the host/hypervisor is the 
adversary, a malicious host can inject partitions into the guest's virtual 
disk. Most critically, injecting a swap partition causes the guest kernel to 
page out TEE-encrypted memory to a host-controlled block device, breaking the 
confidentiality guarantee of the hardware TEE (AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX).

The PodVM images use a GPT-partitioned disk with dm-verity on the root 
partition. However, the roothash= kernel parameter only disables root 
auto-discovery — non-root partitions (swap, /home, /var, /srv, /var/tmp) are 
still auto-discovered and mounted. The generator is shipped unmasked in the 
RHEL systemd-udev subpackage, and no kernel command line parameter in the 
measured UKI addon disables it. Additionally, the PodVM measurement script 
captures PCRs 3, 9, 11, and 12, but not PCR 5 (GPT partition table), so 
partition table modifications are not detected by remote attestation.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nfsd: preflight SEQUENCE replies before accepting a slot

nfsd4_sequence() narrows the reply buffer to the session's cached
reply limit before it accepts the slot seqid. A client may negotiate
ca_maxresponsesize_cached down to NFSD_MIN_HDR_SEQ_SZ, and
nfsd4_alloc_slot() then gives every slot a zero-length sl_data[]. A
COMPOUND tag can fill that narrowed buffer until it holds the
SEQUENCE opcode but not the status word that follows.
nfsd4_encode_operation() returns without running
nfsd4_encode_sequence(), so cstate.data_offset stays zero. It leaves
op->status at nfs_ok as well, so the COMPOUND is treated as having
succeeded.

nfsd4_store_cache_entry() declines to cache a lone SEQUENCE that
returned an error. That test reads the status the operation
reported, so it passes here. The copy starts at offset zero and
takes the whole reply, RPC and COMPOUND headers included, into the
zero-length sl_data[]. The COMPOUND tag is copied along with it, so
the client picks most of the bytes written past the end of the slot:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in read_bytes_from_xdr_buf+0x1bc/0x390
  Write of size 80 at addr ffff888003a549cd by task kunit_try_catch/24
   __asan_memcpy+0x38/0x60
   read_bytes_from_xdr_buf+0x1bc/0x390
   nfsd4_sequence_done+0x5b0/0x810
   nfs4svc_encode_compoundres+0x1bf/0x240

Check that the fixed-size SEQUENCE result, plus room for a following
operation's error status, fits the negotiated limit before narrowing
the buffer and consuming the slot seqid. The slot and its reply
cache are left unchanged, as RFC 8881 Section 2.10.6.1.2 requires of
an error returned from SEQUENCE.

A flaw was found in crun. When copying files onto a tmpfs mounted with tmpcopyup, crun opens the destination a second time by name. A container that shares a writable volume with the container being created can change that path between the two lookups, so crun copies image files onto host files, including files under /proc/sys.

Certain EZVIZ devices are affected by a replay attack vulnerability (CWE-294). An attacker may intercept communication traffic and replay specific control commands, causing the device to execute unauthorized operations.

MemberPress Members before 3.3.1, with the Block Permissions add-on enabled, contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated Author-level users to crash pages by saving a non-string blockPermissionsMessage block attribute. Attackers can store a JSON array in the attribute so wpautop() in get_block_replacement_content() throws a PHP 8 TypeError, causing fatal errors on post, home, search, and REST pages for unauthorized viewers.

dsniff through 2.5a2 contains an integer underflow in decode_sniffer() in decode_sniffer.c that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to write past the global obuf buffer. Attackers can send a UDP datagram to port 2001 on a monitored segment with a 4096-byte string, disabling base64_pton bounds checks to corrupt memory and crash dsniff.

Wfuzz through 3.1.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows malicious target servers to inject script by returning crafted links written unescaped into HTML reports. When the links script and html printer are used, attacker-supplied href values close the unquoted anchor tag and execute JavaScript when the operator opens the report.

Ground Station before 0.8.25 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated non-administrator operators to write files outside data/decoded via the post_process_pipeline value. Attackers can insert ../ sequences into a scheduled observation's IQ task configuration so SatDump creates directories, overwrites same-named files, and recursively deletes created trees on failure.

Donetick before 0.1.86 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the GET /api/v1/assets/*filepath route that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass URL signature checks by prefixing paths with profiles/. Attackers who know a private upload's storage key can request profiles/../users/<id>/<uuid>.<ext> to retrieve private attachments without a signature or login.

VoidAuth before 1.19.2 contains an insufficient session expiration vulnerability that allows attackers to retain account access because the POST /reset_password/passkey/end handler never calls endUserSessions(). Attackers holding a stolen session cookie keep authenticated access to the victim's account even after the victim recovers it by registering a new passkey.

Zipline before 4.8.3 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated OIDC users to make the server fetch arbitrary URLs via the userinfo picture claim. Attackers who control their picture claim at the identity provider can force fetchToDataURL() to request internal or cloud-metadata URLs and read responses from their stored avatar.

OpenOLAT 20.2.2 before 20.3.12, 21.0.0 before 21.0.7, and 21.1.0 before 21.1.2 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the TranscodingDeliveryDispatcher notifyResult callback endpoint. Unauthenticated attackers can POST crafted TranscoderJobResult JSON with attacker-supplied URLs to overwrite transcoded video and audio files and force server-side requests.

binary-parser before 2.3.1 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers controlling parser definitions to inject JavaScript through string-typed options passed unvalidated by Context.generateOption(). Attackers can supply crafted length, lengthInBytes, key, tag, offset, or namely() alias values to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the Node.js process when the parser is compiled.

oasdiff 1.24.0 before 1.34.1 fails to enforce --allow-external-refs=false when --open is used, because the recordingReader() capture reader in load/capture.go never applies the external-reference policy. Attackers supplying an untrusted OpenAPI spec can use external $ref values to read local files or trigger HTTP requests, with contents uploaded in the review bundle.

Kitty 0.43.0 before 0.51.0 contains a terminal escape sequence injection vulnerability that allows attackers to emit escape sequences by crafting malicious file or archive member names. When a victim highlights such an entry in the choose-files kitten preview panel, unsanitized names are written raw, enabling OSC 52 clipboard overwrites, OSC 8 links, window title changes, or screen spoofing.

Lightdash before 3.212.0 contains an insufficiently protected credentials vulnerability in getGitlabInstallationRepoReadAccess that sends the organization GitLab app token to unverified hosts. Project developers can set the dbt connection host_domain to an attacker-controlled server and capture the token when the AI agent reads the repository, gaining access to every reachable repository.

Vim 9.2.0405 before 9.2.1352 contains a security bypass vulnerability in expand_tag_fname() that allows attackers to evade 'tagsecure' URL checks by escaping URLs in tags file entries. Attackers can supply a crafted tags file in a cloned repository so that jumping to a tag makes netrw fetch an attacker-controlled URL leaking environment variable values.

Dashy 4.0.0 before 4.9.12 contains a credential disclosure vulnerability in isLocalRequest that attaches user credentials to lookalike hosts due to prefix-only origin checks. Attackers can lure logged-in users to a crafted ?config= link pointing to a lookalike host, capturing bearer tokens or HTTP auth headers to read configuration and stored API keys, or modify them when the victim is an admin.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in PLYImporter::LoadFace and PLYImporter::createFromeTriStrip that fails to validate face vertex indices against the vertex count. Attackers can supply a crafted PLY file whose out-of-range indices cause GenVertexNormalsProcess::GenMeshVertexNormals to write normals outside the heap buffer, crashing the application or potentially enabling code execution.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an invalid pointer dereference vulnerability in glTFImporter::ImportEmbeddedTextures that derives the texture format hint without checking the strchr result. Attackers can supply a crafted glTF 1.0 file with an embedded image mime type lacking a slash to crash the importing application.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in ColladaParser::ReadPrimitives that allows attackers to exhaust memory via non-numeric index values. Attackers can supply a crafted Collada file whose

index list contains a non-digit character, causing endless zero-index appends until the importing process crashes.

Umbraco CMS 17.4.0 before 17.8.2 and 18.0.0 before 18.3.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability because MemberValueSetBuilder.GetValueSets writes sensitive member properties into the Examine members index. Wing FTP Server before 8.2.8 contains a predictable session identifier vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to hijack administrator sessions by deriving identifiers from process, time, ServerID, and client IP state. ZITADEL 4.19.5 before 4.20.3 contains a host header injection vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect notification links by placing a trusted host in the userinfo portion of the x-zitadel-public-host header. A flaw was found in gpgme. When processing crafted input, an early return following memory reallocation can leave internal buffer pointers referencing previously freed memory, resulting in a double-free condition during cleanup. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability to corrupt process memory, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution or a Denial of Service (DoS) crash.

Kerberos Agent before 3.14.4 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to forge administrator tokens because JWTMiddleWare() falls back to the hard-coded key TOBECHANGED. Attackers can sign HS256 tokens with arbitrary username and role claims to access /api and /config routes, exposing RTSP, ONVIF, Hub and encryption keys, rewriting configuration, and stopping the camera.

AiSOC before 23.6.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the agents service that allows authenticated users to read other tenants' investigation runs by supplying their run_id. Attackers can query GET /api/v1/investigations/{run_id}, report variants, the WebSocket stream, or agent-runs routes to obtain audit logs, forensic output, and incident reports.

Attackers can request the assigned-user-details endpoint to obtain bearer tokens in CustomHeaders and impersonate other users against the downstream MCP server.

KindleEar 3.0.0 through 3.5.3 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows authenticated non-admin users to run Python code by uploading malicious recipes. Attackers can submit crafted recipe source to the /recipe/upload action, which calibre compile_recipe executes via exec() without sandboxing, gaining root code execution in the Docker container and access to password hashes.

MediaInfoLib before 26.10 contains an uninitialized pointer dereference vulnerability because the File_Mpeg4_Descriptors constructor leaves the IsCmaf pointer holding stale heap contents. Attackers can supply a crafted MP4 file with an AAC/USAC decoder specific descriptor so File_Usac::Streams_Finish_Conformance_Profile dereferences an invalid address, crashing the application.

MediaInfoLib before 26.10 contains a divide-by-zero vulnerability in TimeCode::FromString() that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying hour-unit timestamps with fewer than three fractional digits. Attackers can craft a TTML file whose begin or end attribute contains such a timestamp, causing MediaInfo or embedding applications to crash with SIGFPE when opened.

A vulnerability was found in humhub questions up to 1.1.5. Affected is an unknown function of the file widgets/views/answer.php of the component QA Module. Performing a manipulation of the argument displayName results in cross site scripting. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used. Upgrading to version 1.1.6 is able to address this issue. The patch is named cdc39878ba457ca71271c1ec3cf05fe025e3e9fc. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component.

DreameHome for Android (com.dreame.smartlife) before 2.6.4.0 contains a download of code without integrity check vulnerability in RnPluginDownloadManager.java that allows network-positioned attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript within the application by replacing React Native feature bundles that are only validated against a client-stored MD5 checksum without publisher authentication. Attackers can replace both the downloaded bundle and its corresponding MD5 metadata to run modified code with the application's permissions and access to its bridge APIs.

A weakness has been identified in FredrikNoren ungit 1.5.30. Affected by this issue is the function credentialsOption of the file source/git-api.js of the component Remote Git API. Executing a manipulation of the argument Remote can lead to os command injection. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

Dynamic Product Gallery for WooCommerce before 3.6.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers with Contributor-level access or above to inject arbitrary JavaScript via the product_id attribute of the [wc_product_dgallery] and [wc_product_dynamic_gallery] shortcodes. The parse_shortcode_product_dynamic_gallery() function passes product_id only through esc_attr(), and get_gallery_main() prints it unescaped into the a3-wc-dynamic-gallery-init-inline-script inline script as part of a JavaScript variable name, so a value such as 342;alert(document.domain)// breaks out of the declaration. The injected script executes in the browser of any user who views the post, including editors or administrators who preview or approve it.

Hermes Agent is an open-source autonomous AI agent built by Nous Research for running tool-using workflows across CLI, desktop, and messaging interfaces. From 0.21.6 to 0.23.1, when Bot Desktop is hosted inside a non-local terminal backend, the agent process reads a backend-writable screen environment file without validating keys or values and merges its entries into the environment of processes started on the agent machine. Specifically, when terminal.backend is set to docker or ssh (or a plugin backend declaring supports_streams) with placement auto or terminal, _published() in tools/bot_desktop/sandbox_host.py accepts arbitrary KEY=VALUE lines from the hermes-bot-desktop env file and propagates them via tools/bot_desktop/runtime.py into the browser harness, computer-use helpers, and local terminal children. Code running inside the terminal backend can therefore set variables such as LD_PRELOAD, DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES, or PATH and gain code execution on the agent machine as the gateway user upon a subsequent browser or computer-use spawn, exposing credentials, tokens, and session history under the Hermes home directory. The default local backend, backends that cannot host a screen (Modal, Daytona, and Vercel), and Hermes Cloud in its default configuration are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 0.23.2.

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit 118facd, contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the public POST /runner/draft/runner endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to overwrite another participant's saved draft and obtain its private invitation token. The draft save handler in RunnerController and AnswerService loads an existing draft by invitation alone without checking that the submitted survey, participation group and invitation belong together, then replaces the draft's answers, reassigns it to the submitted survey, and returns a resume link containing the private invitation token.

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit de1145c, contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the public POST /editcontribution/{code} endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to overwrite another respondent's submitted answers. The handler in ContributionController selects the survey and answer set from body parameters by numeric contribution ID and never checks that the private edit code in the URL matches that contribution, so an attacker who knows a contribution ID can replace its saved answers without the respondent's edit link.

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit 03cc974, contains a blind server-side request forgery vulnerability in PDF export that allows authenticated attackers with the Form Manager role to make the server send HTTP or HTTPS requests to internal services. Question titles saved through POST /{shortname}/management/edit are rendered as raw markup in runnercontentinnerpdf.jsp, and the PDFRenderer resource loader fetches referenced images without checking whether the destination is on an internal network when a response is exported as a PDF.

OpenEMR is a free and open source electronic health records and medical practice management application. Prior to 8.5.0, the staff-facing portal endpoints GET api/onsiteactivityviews and GET api/onsiteactivityview/{id}, mapped to OnsiteActivityView.Query and OnsiteActivityView.Read with p_acl = p_none in portal/patient/_app_config.php, are handled without an authorization check for an authenticated staff session whose bootstrap_pid is empty. portal/patient/_machine_config.php admits that authenticated staff session, and portal/patient/fwk/libs/verysimple/Phreeze/GenericRouter.php applies the route ACL only when bootstrap_pid is nonempty, so the staff request bypasses the p_none check. OnsiteActivityViewController::Query() returns records without patient scoping, and OnsiteActivityViewController::Read() loads a record by identifier without checking ACL or ownership; OnsiteActivityViewReporter::GetCustomQuery() joins portal activity to patient demographics and includes names, dates of birth, addresses, and Social Security numbers. Any authenticated staff account, including one without the patients/demo permission, can therefore read sensitive demographics for patients represented by an existing onsite_portal_activity row; at least one such row must exist for the endpoint to return patient data. This issue is fixed in version 8.5.0.

TastyIgniter is an open-source online ordering, table reservation, and restaurant management system. Prior to 4.2.0, the User extension’s onRequestResetPassword() handler in src/Http/Controllers/Login.php calls resetPassword() and mailSendResetPasswordRequest() only when an account matches. The resulting database write and reset-email send take longer than the nonexistent-account path despite the endpoint returning the same response, allowing timing measurements against a production deployment using a synchronous queue and real SMTP transport to disclose valid staff or customer email addresses. The advisory’s local log-mailer test showed no measurable timing difference, so the signal depends on mail configuration and is useful for follow-on phishing or credential stuffing rather than direct account access. This issue is fixed in version 4.2.0.

A vulnerability has been found in D-Link DIR-600L 2.17b02. Affected by this vulnerability is the function hedwigcgi_main of the file hedwig.cgi. The manipulation leads to missing authentication. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used.

An information disclosure vulnerability in Zstandard versions 1.5.1 through 1.5.7 allows specially crafted compressed data to expose the contents of an internal buffer through decompressed output. The buffer is 64 KiB in the default configuration and may contain uninitialized memory or literals from earlier decompressions performed using the same decompression context. An attacker who can submit compressed data and observe the resulting output can recover the buffer's contents.

Trilium through 0.107.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability in updateNormalEntity() that allows malicious sync partners to inject SQL by supplying crafted entity names and column keys. Attackers can abuse /api/sync/changed or PUT /api/sync/update data to copy sessions, etapi_tokens and user_data into synced rows and write arbitrary database rows.

Open5GS WebUI through 2.8.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in webui/server/routes/db.js that allows authenticated user-role accounts to modify the Account model. Attackers can send PATCH /api/db/Account/<username> setting roles to admin, overwrite password hashes, delete accounts, and read hashes to gain full administrative control.

rConfig Core 8.0.0 before 8.2.13 and rConfig Pro before 8.4.0 contain an authorization bypass vulnerability in the users API that allows authenticated users to modify other accounts. Attackers can send a UserController::update request with an administrator's user id and new password, then log in as that administrator to take full control.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.7.1 through 0.8.4, an incomplete IPv6 blocklist in AutoGPT's outbound SSRF protection allows authenticated users to reach local or private network services. Specifically, _is_ip_blocked and BLOCKED_IP_NETWORKS in autogpt_platform/backend/backend/util/request.py fail to reject the IPv6 unspecified address :: (which connects to ::1 on Linux) as well as 6to4, NAT64, Teredo, and deprecated IPv4-compatible IPv6 encodings. An attacker can pass :: directly to blocks/sql_query_block.py or blocks/email_block.py, or point URL-fetching blocks, web fetch, MCP servers, webhooks, or OAuth at a hostname whose AAAA record resolves to ::. On backends run directly on a host, this exposes unauthenticated internal RPC services and databases listening on ::1, though the default Docker Compose and single-container deployments bind internal services to IPv4 only. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

A flaw has been found in amirhamza05 Student-Management-System up to 449397e35d42e3779f14f0bfc654ab307103f7e3. This issue affects some unknown processing of the file page_action/user/user_profile.php of the component User Profile Handler. This manipulation causes authorization bypass. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. Continious delivery with rolling releases is used by this product. Therefore, no version details of affected nor updated releases are available. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the MXG demuxer's mxg_read_packet() that allows attackers to leak uninitialized heap memory through truncated marker segments. Attackers can supply a crafted MXG file ending in a truncated APP13 segment with a large declared length, causing uninitialized heap contents to be emitted as audio packet payload, for example into remuxed output files.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a stack out-of-bounds read vulnerability in ff_h264_parse_framesize() in libavformat/rtpdec_h264.c when parsing an SDP a=framesize attribute lacking a height. Attackers controlling an RTSP server DESCRIBE response or a crafted .sdp file can make atoi() read past the line buffer, crashing clients or parsing stale stack bytes.

FFmpeg 8.0 before 9.1 contains an improper URL scheme validation vulnerability in the WHIP muxer that allows malicious WHIP servers to create or truncate local files via the Location header. Attackers can return a file: URL that dispose_session() opens read-write with truncation on teardown, destroying arbitrary user-writable files or redirecting requests to other protocols.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in libavformat/mmst.c that allows malicious MMS servers to crash clients by sending malformed ASF headers. Attackers can send an ASF header lacking a packet size or stream properties, causing mms_open() to return success after freeing state and crash on first read.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in amf_get_field_value2() in libavformat/rtmppkt.c that NUL-terminates truncated AMF strings at the declared length instead of bytes read. A malicious RTMP server, or connecting client in listen mode, can send truncated onStatus or _error strings to leak uninitialized stack memory through log messages.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in the AVIF muxer in libavformat/movenc.c that allows attackers to crash the application through streams with unknown pixel formats. Attackers can supply a crafted input whose video stream is stream-copied to AVIF, causing unchecked av_pix_fmt_desc_get() results to be dereferenced, resulting in denial of service.

FFmpeg 8.0 before 9.1 contains a use of uninitialized memory vulnerability in opus_parse_packet() in libavformat/rtpdec_opus.c that reads the Opus TOC byte from stale buffer memory when parsing empty RTP payloads. A malicious RTSP server or RTP sender can deliver an empty Opus payload to cause incorrect packet durations and leak bits of stale memory through pkt->duration.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in ff_rtp_send_vc2hq() in libavformat/rtpenc_vc2hq.c that accepts a Dirac next parse offset of zero. Attackers can supply crafted Dirac/VC-2 video remuxed to the RTP muxer, causing the parsing pointer to never advance and consume CPU indefinitely.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in peak_init_writer() and wav_write_packet() in libavformat/wavenc.c that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying audio with zero channels. Attackers can provide a crafted PCM stream declaring no channels for WAV output with peak envelope enabled, causing out-of-bounds writes past peak_maxpos and peak_maxneg arrays, crashes, and potential code execution.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in rdt_parse_packet() in libavformat/rdt.c that allows remote attackers to crash applications by omitting the ASMRuleBook SDP attribute. Attackers can serve an RTSP session selecting RDT transport without ASMRuleBook, then send an RDT data packet to crash ffmpeg or ffprobe.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an integer overflow in send_picture() of libavformat/rtpenc_vc2hq.c that leaves the bit reader without a buffer, causing a NULL pointer dereference. Attackers can supply a Dirac/VC-2 stream with a picture data unit of about 256 MiB or more to crash applications packetizing it to RTP.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in filter_slice_rgba_planar() that allows attackers to read beyond lookup tables using unmasked high bit depth planar samples. Attackers can supply crafted video with samples exceeding the nominal depth, passed unchanged by rawvideo, to crash the application or leak heap contents into output video.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in libavfilter/vf_readeia608.c because build_histogram() does not clamp high bit depth luma samples to the nominal maximum. Attackers can supply crafted 9, 10, 12 or 14 bit gray or YUV video to corrupt heap memory, causing crashes or possibly code execution.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the lut1d filter in libavfilter/vf_lut3d.c that allows attackers to read heap memory by supplying planar high bit depth samples above the nominal depth. Attackers can craft 9, 10, 12 or 14 bit planar RGB video processed with a large 1D LUT to crash applications or disclose heap contents in output pixels.

c-icap-server through 0.5.15 and 0.6.5 contains an out-of-bounds write in process_encapsulated() that allows unauthenticated attackers to corrupt heap memory by sending six Encapsulated entities. Attackers can send a single ICAP request whose sixth entity overwrites trash_entities[0], triggering use-after-free and double free in ci_request_destroy() during teardown.

Pangolin before 1.21.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in isPathAllowed() in server/lib/pathMatch.ts that splits paths on literal slashes without percent-decoding or resolving dot segments. TypiCMS Core before 17.0.46 contains an insufficiently protected credentials vulnerability that allows authenticated users with "read users" permission to view plaintext api_token values for all users, including superusers, via the GET /api/users endpoint. Attackers can steal a superuser's non-expiring, non-rotatable api_token from the JSON response and use it to gain full superuser API access, enabling creation and deletion of users, roles, and all content.

Attackers can call /api/python/execute or /api/process/execute-async to run Python scripts and commands as the server user, even via malicious web pages abusing permissive CORS against loopback instances.

The modal_content_ajax_callback() handler for the merchant_quick_view_content AJAX action is registered for unauthenticated users, is gated only by the merchant-nonce value exposed to every front-end visitor, and loads any supplied product_id with wc_get_product() without checking the product's post status or the user's read_post capability. Attackers can iterate product IDs to obtain the title, price, description, gallery images, and SKU of unpublished products when the Quick View module is enabled.

descriptions.value: Pion DTLS is a Go implementation of Datagram Transport Layer Security. From 2.1.0 until 3.1.14, a server with a SessionStore saved the session ID and master secret after ClientKeyExchange, before receiving a valid Finished message and before enforcing the configured client-authentication checks. A remote client can omit its Certificate message, send ClientKeyExchange, leave the first handshake unfinished, and then resume the cached session using the master secret it learned during key exchange. The server must use a SessionStore and negotiate a certificate-based cipher suite. The attack can bypass client certificates required through RequireAnyClientCert or RequireAndVerifyClientCert, or a rejecting VerifyConnection callback. WebRTC users are not affected. The abbreviated handshake can allow unauthorized access to application data. The issue is fixed in version 3.1.14.

Pion DTLS is a Go implementation of Datagram Transport Layer Security. From 1.2.2 until 3.1.13, the server state machine did not distinguish successful processing of the client certificate flight from completion of the handshake, so later traffic could revisit the same cached Certificate, ClientKeyExchange, and CertificateVerify messages. A malicious client can withhold Finished and send additional handshake traffic. Depending on the configured authentication policy, repeated work can include certificate parsing, handshake signature verification, and certificate-chain verification. The vulnerable endpoint must act as the DTLS server. Pion WebRTC applications are affected when they operate in that role. Repeated or concurrent attempts can consume excessive CPU resources, delay legitimate connections, and reduce service availability. The issue is fixed in version 3.1.13.

Listdom by Webilia plugin for WordPress before 6.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers with Contributor-level access or above to retrieve the email address and user ID of every registered user. Attackers can exploit the LSD_Ajax::autosuggest() handler by setting the source parameter to users and repeating requests with different term values to enumerate the full user base, including administrators, bypassing the 10-result limit.

cnpmcore 3.46.0 before 3.84.3 and 4.0.0 before 4.37.3 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain upstream registry authTokens via the GET /-/registry endpoints lacking AdminAccess middleware. Attackers can request /-/registry or /-/registry/:id and replay the leaked authToken as a Bearer credential to enumerate, download, or publish packages upstream.

Prismor before 1.57.0 contains a wildcard CORS misconfiguration and missing authentication in its local HTTP API that allows remote attackers to overwrite security policies via cross-origin requests. Attackers can lure a developer to a malicious page that sends PUT requests to /api/policy/global or /api/policy/project, disabling AI agent guardrails and reading session and event data.

RayLabsHQ gitea-mirror before 3.38.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the /api/sso/providers handlers that allows any authenticated user to access other users' SSO providers without ownership checks. Attackers can read every OIDC client secret in clear text and overwrite or delete providers, redirecting authorization and token endpoints to attacker-controlled servers.

GPAC through 26.07.0 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in gf_rtp_parse_amr that allows remote RTP senders or malicious RTSP servers to read beyond packet buffers by sending crafted AMR/AMR-WB payloads. Attackers can send short packets whose TOC entries all set the F bit, causing out-of-bounds frame data to be copied into decoder output, disclosing memory or crashing the client.

libical before 4.0.7 contains a denial of service vulnerability because icalparser_clean() does not reset the parser nesting level when reusing an icalparser. Attackers can submit a single malformed calendar with unclosed or mismatched BEGIN/END lines, causing later calendars to be silently dropped and memory to grow unbounded.

A low-privileged attacker could exploit this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code. Exploitation of this issue does not require user interaction. Scope is changed.

BusyBox through 1.38.0 contains an absolute path traversal vulnerability in tftpd that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to access files outside any intended directory when started without a DIR argument. Attackers can send RRQ or WRQ packets with file names beginning with '/' to read sensitive files like /etc/shadow or overwrite files, typically as root.

VeraCrypt before 1.26.30 on Linux contains a command injection vulnerability in CoreUnix::CheckFilesystem that allows a local attacker with same-UID access and an active elevated CoreService session to execute arbitrary commands by injecting an unsanitized VirtualDevice value into a shell command string. Attackers can reopen the request pipe through /proc/<pid>/fd/<n> and supply a crafted VirtualDevice value such as /dev/null; <command> to achieve arbitrary command execution as root.

VeraCrypt through 1.26.31 on Linux contains an improper path restriction vulnerability in the elevated CoreService, which passes the path and owner UID from a SetFileOwnerRequest directly to chown() in CoreUnix::SetFileOwner without target validation on Linux. An attacker with an active elevated CoreService session and same-UID access who reopens the request pipe through /proc/<pid>/fd/<n> can take ownership of arbitrary system files such as /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow, achieving full root compromise.

Strong::Random versions through 0.96 for Perl allow every later rand output to be predicted from three earlier ones.

The generator keeps its state in a single number. Each call multiplies the state by a factor derived from it, and the returned digits encode that factor, so three consecutive outputs determine the state however the generator was seeded. Outputs are also biased: the first digit after the decimal point is never zero, so rand(256) never returns 1 to 24.

An attacker who sees three consecutive outputs can predict the tokens, passwords or key bytes that the same object later issues to other users.
